subject: general
question: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1973**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Project Tiger** was launched by the Government of India on **1st April 1973**.
 
• The aim of this initiative was to ensure a viable population of Bengal tigers in their natural habitats and to protect them from extinction.
 
• This project is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).
 
• Initially, nine tiger reserves were covered under this project, which has now expanded to cover more than 50 tiger reserves across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**

 
 
• The NTCA was constituted under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, as amended in 2006, for strengthening tiger conservation.
 
• It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
 
• The NTCA is responsible for the implementation of Project Tiger to ensure the protection of tigers.
 
• It regularly assesses tiger populations, habitat status, and the success of conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**
 
 
• This Act was enacted by the Indian Parliament to ensure the protection of wild animals, birds, and plants.
 
• It aims to safeguard the country's ecological and environmental security.
 
• The Act provides for the creation of protected areas such as national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.
 
• It also lays down the legal framework for the protection and management of wildlife habitats.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Bengal Tigers**
 
 
• Bengal tigers (Panthera tigris tigris) are native to the Indian subcontinent and are classified as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
 
• Efforts to conserve Bengal tigers include anti-poaching measures, habitat restoration, and community involvement.
 
• India is home to more than 70% of the world's wild tiger population.
 
• Effective conservation strategies have led to an increase in the tiger population in recent years.
